enonce_markdown: A salesman earns a commission of $15\%$ on goods worth $24{,}000$ FCFA that he has sold. His commission is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

To find a percentage of a quantity, multiply the quantity by the percentage written as a fraction over $100$.

### Solution

Commission $= \dfrac{15}{100} \times 24\,000 = 15 \times 240 = 3\,600$ FCFA.

Common errors: $360$ is only $1.5\%$ ($15 \times 24$); $1{,}600$ is $24\,000 \div 15$; $36$ is the result of a decimal-place slip.

**Answer: 3,600 FCFA.**

enonce_markdown: A tailor in Douala buys a sewing machine for $80{,}000$ FCFA and sells it for $100{,}000$ FCFA. Her percentage profit is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Profit $=$ selling price $-$ cost price, and percentage profit $= \dfrac{\text{profit}}{\text{cost price}} \times 100\%$. The percentage is always taken on the cost price.

### Solution

Profit $= 100\,000 - 80\,000 = 20\,000$ FCFA.

Percentage profit $= \dfrac{20\,000}{80\,000} \times 100\% = 25\%$.

Common errors: $20\%$ takes the profit over the selling price; $80\%$ is the cost price as a percentage of the selling price; $125\%$ is the selling price as a percentage of the cost price.

**Answer: 25%.**

enonce_markdown: After a reduction of $20\%$ in a sale, a handbag costs $28{,}000$ FCFA. The original price of the handbag was
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

This is a reverse percentage. After a $20\%$ reduction the new price is $80\%$ of the original price, so original price $=\dfrac{\text{new price}}{0.80}$. Do not take $20\%$ of the new price.

### Solution

New price $= 100\% - 20\% = 80\%$ of the original price.

$80\% \text{ of original} = 28\,000$, so $1\% = 28\,000 \div 80 = 350$ and $100\% = 35\,000$.

Check: $20\%$ of $35\,000 = 7\,000$ and $35\,000 - 7\,000 = 28\,000$.

Common errors: $22{,}400$ takes $80\%$ of the new price; $33{,}600$ adds $20\%$ of the new price; $140{,}000$ divides by $20\%$ instead of $80\%$.

**Answer: 35,000 FCFA.**

enonce_markdown:
A farmer in Bamenda borrows $350{,}000$ FCFA from a cooperative at a simple interest rate of $6\%$ per year for $4$ years.

(a) Calculate the simple interest he pays.

(b) Calculate the total amount he must repay.

(c) Another farmer invests $200{,}000$ FCFA and earns a simple interest of $36{,}000$ FCFA in $3$ years. Find the yearly rate of interest.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Simple interest is $I = \dfrac{P \times R \times T}{100}$, where $P$ is the amount, $R$ the yearly rate in percent and $T$ the time in years. The total repaid is $P + I$. To find a rate, rearrange: $R = \dfrac{100 \times I}{P \times T}$.

### Solution

**(a)** $I = \dfrac{350\,000 \times 6 \times 4}{100} = 3\,500 \times 24 = 84\,000$ FCFA.

**(b)** Total repaid $= 350\,000 + 84\,000 = 434\,000$ FCFA.

**(c)** $R = \dfrac{100 \times 36\,000}{200\,000 \times 3} = \dfrac{3\,600\,000}{600\,000} = 6$.

Check: $\dfrac{200\,000 \times 6 \times 3}{100} = 36\,000$. Correct.

**Answers: (a) 84,000 FCFA; (b) 434,000 FCFA; (c) 6% per year.**

enonce_markdown: A traveller changes $210{,}000$ FCFA into US dollars at the rate of $1$ dollar $= 600$ FCFA. The number of dollars he receives is
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

To change into a currency that is worth more per unit, divide by the exchange rate (the FCFA value of one unit). Multiply only when converting the other way, from dollars into FCFA.

### Solution

Number of dollars $= \dfrac{210\,000}{600} = 350$.

Check: $350 \times 600 = 210\,000$ FCFA.

Common errors: $126{,}000{,}000$ comes from multiplying instead of dividing; $3{,}500$ and $35{,}000$ come from misplacing the decimal point when dividing.

**Answer: 350 dollars.**

enonce_markdown:
A television set has a cash price of $180{,}000$ FCFA. A shop also sells it on hire purchase: a deposit of $20\%$ of the cash price, followed by $12$ monthly instalments of $14{,}000$ FCFA each.

(a) Calculate the deposit.

(b) Calculate the total hire purchase price.

(c) How much more does a customer pay by hire purchase than by paying cash?

(d) Express your answer to (c) as a percentage of the cash price, correct to 1 decimal place.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Hire purchase price $=$ deposit $+$ (number of instalments $\times$ instalment). The extra cost is the hire purchase price minus the cash price, and a percentage of the cash price is $\dfrac{\text{extra}}{\text{cash price}} \times 100\%$.

### Solution

**(a)** Deposit $= \dfrac{20}{100} \times 180\,000 = 36\,000$ FCFA.

**(b)** Instalments: $12 \times 14\,000 = 168\,000$ FCFA.

Hire purchase price $= 36\,000 + 168\,000 = 204\,000$ FCFA.

**(c)** Extra $= 204\,000 - 180\,000 = 24\,000$ FCFA.

**(d)** $\dfrac{24\,000}{180\,000} \times 100\% = 13.3\%$ (1 d.p.).

**Answers: (a) 36,000 FCFA; (b) 204,000 FCFA; (c) 24,000 FCFA; (d) 13.3%.**
